=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged working advice – for discussion with Australian-qualified transaction counsel before issuing a mark-up.

## 1. Overall read

The Seller's cover note calls the package "fair and balanced". It is not. Read as a whole, the SPA Update does three things that cut hard against a buyer paying AUD 24m on a debt-free/cash-free basis:

1. **It collapses every category of claim into one low, short, heavily-thresholded regime** (20% cap, 18 months, deductible basket) and then sweeps title, tax, IP, indemnities and "all Claims of any nature" into it.
2. **It converts the warranty package into near-nothing via disclosure and knowledge** – general disclosure of the whole data room plus public registers, and a "discoverable" constructive-knowledge bar in cl 8.3.
3. **It pushes known, quantified, Completion-triggered liabilities past Completion** (Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k + IP, Bluefen consent conditions) so they land in the Company after we own it.

Usefully, the Disclosure Letter is more candid than the SPA Update and repeatedly contradicts it (e.g. "Bluefen consent is addressed" vs. "no final written consent included"). Those inconsistencies should be used in the mark-up.

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

### A. Liability architecture (cl 12.1–12.3, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

| Seller position | Problem for Buyer | Recommended position |
|---|---|---|
| **Cap 20% (AUD 4.8m) for general warranties** | Low end of Australian mid-market, and the real exposures identified in DD (Bluefen ~AUD 3.6m revenue, Riverlark 3.2m, incident, IP) could individually exhaust it. | Open at 50–100%; land no lower than 30–40% unless W&I insurance is procured, in which case Seller cap can drop but only with a clean, bound policy and Seller still carrying retention/known matters. |
| **De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, excess-only (deductible)** | Deductible basket means the first AUD 250k of loss is never recovered. 25k de minimis combined with a "related claims" gap invites splitting (see Sandbar). | Tipping basket (first dollar recoverable once exceeded); de minimis ~AUD 10–15k; aggregation of claims arising from the same or related facts; **no thresholds** for Fundamental/Title, Tax, or Specific Indemnities. |
| **18 months for all general warranties; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | 18 months is tolerable for operational warranties only if Completion Accounts and one full audit cycle fall within it. The default-sweep sentence is the real danger: it drags indemnity, leakage, Completion-adjustment and fraud claims into the caps and time bar by default. | 18–24 months general; **Tax 7 years** post-Completion (aligns with ATO amendment periods); Fundamental/Title 6 years or unlimited. Reverse the default: limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and *only* where expressly stated. |
| **Fundamental/title/capacity subject to same caps and time limits ("administrative simplicity")** | Unjustifiable. If title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing and can recover 4.8m. | Reject outright. Title/capacity: cap = 100% of price (plus costs), no de minimis/basket, 6+ years. |
| **Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"** | Would purport to exclude fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities, leakage, price adjustment disputes, and claims under *Australian Consumer Law* s 18 (misleading or deceptive conduct – which cannot be contractually excluded in any event, so the clause is also partly ineffective). | Express carve-outs: fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct/concealment; Specific Indemnities; Tax Indemnity; leakage; Completion Accounts/adjustment; Fundamental Warranties. Non-reliance to be mutual-knowledge-based and not to extend to the Disclosure Letter or Warranties themselves. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge (Schedule 7, Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2, cl 8.3)

- **General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2).** This is the single largest value leak in the package. A buyer cannot be taken to have been "disclosed" a document merely because it exists in a 10-folder VDR. Push for a **fair disclosure standard**: disclosed only if the fact, matter or circumstance is disclosed in the Disclosure Letter (or in a specifically indexed document) *with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect*. Delete general disclosure of public registers (ASIC, PPSR, court lists) entirely, or limit it to specified searches on a specified date which we have actually run.
- **Freeze the data room.** DL 1.1 fixes 5pm 22 Sept 2026. Require an agreed index, a sealed copy (USB/escrow) and a covenant that nothing is added or treated as disclosed thereafter. The Seller's own DL confirms the room was *incomplete* on at least four key matters (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay receipt/assignment, incident investigation) – so "everything in the data room" cannot cure those gaps.
- **Cl 8.3 Buyer knowledge – "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".** Constructive knowledge of anything "discoverable" effectively deletes the warranties: the Seller would argue every breach could have been found by someone. Position: delete; fall-back is *actual* knowledge of a short list of named Wattlebridge individuals of a matter *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter, with no deemed/constructive knowledge and no imputation of advisers' knowledge. Note the DL's own para 10 concedes we have *not* completed verification – which cuts against any deemed-knowledge argument.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission)** is standard, but ensure it cannot be read as preventing a disclosed matter from grounding a Specific Indemnity claim – disclosure should qualify warranties only, never indemnities.

### C. Known matters pushed past Completion – the "closing leakage" cluster

**1. Riverlark Bank facility – ~AUD 3.2m (cl 2/7, DD-003).**
"Release to be provided following Completion" is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal and leaves the Company (now ours) carrying secured debt in change-of-control default (cl 8.1) on day one. Required:
- Repayment at Completion out of Seller proceeds through the funds flow (payout figure confirmed by bank payout letter); and
- Executed deed of release/discharge, PPSR discharge forms and release of any guarantees delivered **at** Completion, as a Completion deliverable and condition of Buyer's obligation to pay.
- Confirm whether Riverlark security extends to the shares themselves (would also go to title – see F).
- If the mechanics genuinely cannot be completed at Completion, hold the full payout amount in escrow with release only against discharge.

**2. DD-005 Completion bonuses – AUD 420,000.**
These are triggered *by Completion* and are liabilities of the **Company** (employer), not the Seller personally; "a matter for the Seller and not itemised" means we fund them post-Completion. Treat as a Transaction Expense / debt-like item deducted from the price, **grossed up for on-costs** (superannuation guarantee at 12%, NSW payroll tax at 5.45%, plus any leave accrual effect) – indicatively AUD 490–500k. Also clarify: who bears the bonus if the continued-employment condition fails, and are any bonus recipients the people who negotiated the Bluefen/Ironquay matters (retention risk).

**3. Ironquay Development Studio – IP in SOW3 Project Materials (cl 11.1, DD-004, DD-010).**
Under cl 7.3 of the Ironquay contract, IP in the SOW3 deliverables does not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid; DD-010 shows AUD 180k outstanding; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment are in the room. The Seller's indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" misdescribes the risk: the exposure is **not owning IP that is presumably embedded in Paperbark's product**, plus Ironquay's leverage to hold up or claim infringement. Required:
- Pre-Completion covenant / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment **and** an executed confirmatory deed of assignment (with moral-rights consents and delivery of source materials) from Ironquay.
- Specific indemnity covering any defect in title to Project Materials, third-party claims, licence fees, re-development/remediation costs and lost revenue – uncapped or capped at price, outside thresholds, 6-year survival.
- If assignment cannot be delivered by Completion: escrow materially above AUD 180k reflecting the remediation risk.

**4. Bluefen – ~30% of revenue (cl 3/6.3, DD-002).**
The Seller says the consent is "addressed" and will be treated as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent"; the DL admits no consent exists and that cl 11.3 attaches *conditions*. A bare letter will not do. Required:
- CP (for Buyer's benefit, waivable only by Buyer): unconditional written consent from Bluefen in a form reasonably satisfactory to Buyer, **and** evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied or irrevocably waived, with no amendment to pricing/term.
- "Reasonable endeavours" → "all reasonable endeavours"/"best endeavours", with a no-payment-without-Buyer-consent limb (Seller cannot buy the consent by conceding commercial terms that bind the Company post-Completion).
- Price protection if consent is conditional or late: deferred consideration or escrow referenced to Bluefen revenue, and a specific indemnity/termination right if Bluefen terminates for change of control within 12 months.
- Diligence: confirm whether Bluefen's 11.2 is triggered by the share sale (change of control) – the Seller's wording elsewhere (Mossvale) suggests they will argue narrowly; here it is the Seller who concedes consent is needed.

**5. DD-006 export/privacy incident.**
"Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" is the Seller's characterisation only; the DL concedes that unauthorised access, scope and notification are all unresolved. ~1,240 records of personal information sent externally is squarely within the *Privacy Act 1988* Notifiable Data Breaches regime if serious harm is likely, and the current penalty and statutory-tort environment is materially harsher than two years ago. Required:
- Pre-Completion covenant: complete the investigation, make any OAIC/individual notifications required, and provide the full forensic report to Buyer; Buyer consultation right on notification decisions.
- Specific indemnity for all costs, notifications, regulatory penalties/enforceable undertakings, third-party and customer claims (including under Bluefen/Mossvale contracts), and remediation – outside caps and thresholds, 6-year survival.
- Warranties: no other incidents; compliance with APP 11 and contractual security obligations; and a bring-down at Completion with a MAC/termination right if the incident proves to be a significant breach.

**6. Sandbar renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DD-008, DD-011).**
Three "related" renewals of identical amounts split across two documents, with the DL declining to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, is a pattern we should test. Issues: (a) are they accrued in the Accounts/Completion working capital or are they off-balance-sheet commitments? (b) are they genuinely required for the business (if not, a price deduction or Seller-funded termination)? (c) related-party? (d) renewal dates – if they fall before Completion, they are a locked-box/leakage item unless clearly ordinary course. Also use this to reinforce aggregation language in cl 12.2 so the Seller cannot fragment related claims below the de minimis.

### D. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"

Reject. Tax should have (i) a separate tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax (including any payroll tax/SG shortfall on DD-005 and any R&D tax incentive clawback common in analytics businesses), (ii) 7-year survival, (iii) cap at 100% of price, (iv) no thresholds. IP warranties (ownership of core platform IP, open-source compliance, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments) should run at least 3–4 years given the Ironquay evidence that contractor IP has not been properly captured.

### E. Lease and Mossvale (DD-007, DD-009)

Lower risk but tidy up: (a) DD-007 notification to landlord to be given pre-Completion with evidence delivered at Completion; (b) Mossvale – confirm whether there is a separate change-of-control clause beyond the assignment restriction, obtain a comfort letter if practical, and extend the Bluefen-style warranty to "no material contract is terminable or varied by reason of the Transaction".

### F. Title (DD-012)

A share register is prima facie evidence of membership only (*Corporations Act* s 176) – it is not proof that the shares are unencumbered or fully paid, nor of authority to sell. We should run/obtain: ASIC company extract and share-structure history; constitution (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag, share transfer approval); any shareholders' agreement; PPSR search against Harbourglass **and** Paperbark for security over shares; evidence of no options/ESOP/convertible notes; original share certificates (or confirmation none issued); Seller board approval; and FIRB analysis if any Wattlebridge ownership is foreign. Title and capacity warranties uncapped (see A).

### G. Credit risk on the Seller

Harbourglass is a venture vehicle; proceeds may be distributed to LPs shortly after Completion, making any warranty or indemnity worthless in practice. Require **escrow/retention (indicatively 10–15% of price, 18–24 months, with longer tail for Tax/Specific Indemnities)** or a creditworthy parent guarantee, in addition to the specific escrows above. W&I insurance can substitute for part of this but not for the known matters, which an insurer will exclude.

## 3. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

**Must-have (deal-protective)**
1. Riverlark: repaid and fully discharged **at** Completion via funds flow; no post-Completion release. Escrow full amount if not.
2. Fundamental/Title/Capacity and Tax carved out of general regime – 100% cap, no thresholds, 6–7 years.
3. Delete default sweep ("any limitation applies to all Claims") and "all Claims of any nature" in cl 9.3/12.8/20.5; carve out fraud, specific indemnities, tax indemnity, leakage, adjustments.
4. Replace general data-room/public-register disclosure with a fair-disclosure standard; freeze and seal the data room as at 22 Sept 2026.
5. Delete cl 8.3 constructive knowledge; fall-back to actual knowledge of named individuals of matters fairly disclosed.
6. Bluefen: Buyer-only CP for unconditional consent **plus** satisfaction/waiver of cl 11.3 conditions; price protection if conditional.
7. DD-005 bonuses (grossed up for SG/payroll tax, ~AUD 490–500k) treated as Transaction Expense deducted from price.

**Strong push**
8. Ironquay: cleared payment **and** confirmatory IP assignment as Completion deliverable; specific indemnity for IP title defects, not limited to AUD 180k.
9. DD-006 incident: pre-Completion investigation/notification covenant; uncapped specific indemnity; bring-down and MAC right.
10. General cap: open at 50–100%, floor 30–40% absent W&I; tipping basket; lower de minimis; related-claim aggregation.
11. Escrow/retention 10–15% for 18–24 months (longer tail for tax/indemnities) or parent guarantee.

**Clean-up / diligence**
12. Sandbar renewals: determine accrual, necessity and timing; price or working-capital treatment accordingly.
13. Complete independent title verification (ASIC, PPSR, constitution, options/notes, certificates).
14. Lease notification evidence at Completion; Mossvale change-of-control check; general "no contract affected by the Transaction" warranty.
15. Separate tax indemnity and extended IP warranty survival.

**Negotiating note:** the Disclosure Letter's own admissions (paras 2–6, 10) contradict the SPA Update's "addressed / adequate / not material / settled" characterisations. Lead the mark-up with those contradictions – they justify every structural change above without needing to argue market practice.

*This review is based solely on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter as provided; it should be checked against the full SPA draft and underlying DD documents, and figures (e.g. on-costs) confirmed by tax counsel before being relied on in negotiation.*

- Price protection if consent is conditional or late: deferred consideration or escrow referenced to Bluefen revenue, and a specific indemnity/termination right if Bluefen terminates for change of control within 12 months.
- Diligence: confirm whether Bluefen's 11.2 is triggered by the share sale (change of control) – the Seller's wording elsewhere (Mossvale) suggests they will argue narrowly; here it is the Seller who concedes consent is needed.

**5. DD-006 export/privacy incident.**
"Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" is the Seller's characterisation only; the DL concedes that unauthorised access, scope and notification are all unresolved. ~1,240 records of personal information sent externally is squarely within the *Privacy Act 1988* Notifiable Data Breaches regime if serious harm is likely, and the current penalty and statutory-tort environment is materially harsher than two years ago. Required:
- Pre-Completion covenant: complete the investigation, make any OAIC/individual notifications required, and provide the full forensic report to Buyer; Buyer consultation right on notification decisions.
- Specific indemnity for all costs, notifications, regulatory penalties/enforceable undertakings, third-party and customer claims (including under Bluefen/Mossvale contracts), and remediation – outside caps and thresholds, 6-year survival.
- Warranties: no other incidents; compliance with APP 11 and contractual security obligations; and a bring-down at Completion with a MAC/termination right if the incident proves to be a significant breach.

**6. Sandbar renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DD-008, DD-011).**
Three "related" renewals of identical amounts split across two documents, with the DL declining to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, is a pattern we should test. Issues: (a) are they accrued in the Accounts/Completion working capital or are they off-balance-sheet commitments? (b) are they genuinely required for the business (if not, a price deduction or Seller-funded termination)? (c) related-party? (d) renewal dates – if they fall before Completion, they are a locked-box/leakage item unless clearly ordinary course. Also use this to reinforce aggregation language in cl 12.2 so the Seller cannot fragment related claims below the de minimis.

### D. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"

Reject. Tax should have (i) a separate tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax (including any payroll tax/SG shortfall on DD-005 and any R&D tax incentive clawback common in analytics businesses), (ii) 7-year survival, (iii) cap at 100% of price, (iv) no thresholds. IP warranties (ownership of core platform IP, open-source compliance, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments) should run at least 3–4 years given the Ironquay evidence that contractor IP has not been properly captured.

### E. Lease and Mossvale (DD-007, DD-009)

Lower risk but tidy up: (a) DD-007 notification to landlord to be given pre-Completion with evidence delivered at Completion; (b) Mossvale – confirm whether there is a separate change-of-control clause beyond the assignment restriction, obtain a comfort letter if practical, and extend the Bluefen-style warranty to "no material contract is terminable or varied by reason of the Transaction".

### F. Title (DD-012)

A share register is prima facie evidence of membership only (*Corporations Act* s 176) – it is not proof that the shares are unencumbered or fully paid, nor of authority to sell. We should run/obtain: ASIC company extract and share-structure history; constitution (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag, share transfer approval); any shareholders' agreement; PPSR search against Harbourglass **and** Paperbark for security over shares; evidence of no options/ESOP/convertible notes; original share certificates (or confirmation none issued); Seller board approval; and FIRB analysis if any Wattlebridge ownership is foreign. Title and capacity warranties uncapped (see A).

### G. Credit risk on the Seller

Harbourglass is a venture vehicle; proceeds may be distributed to LPs shortly after Completion, making any warranty or indemnity worthless in practice. Require **escrow/retention (indicatively 10–15% of price, 18–24 months, with longer tail for Tax/Specific Indemnities)** or a creditworthy parent guarantee, in addition to the specific escrows above. W&I insurance can substitute for part of this but not for the known matters, which an insurer will exclude.

## 3. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

**Must-have (deal-protective)**
1. Riverlark: repaid and fully discharged **at** Completion via funds flow; no post-Completion release. Escrow full amount if not.
2. Fundamental/Title/Capacity and Tax carved out of general regime – 100% cap, no thresholds, 6–7 years.
3. Delete default sweep ("any limitation applies to all Claims") and "all Claims of any nature" in cl 9.3/12.8/20.5; carve out fraud, specific indemnities, tax indemnity, leakage, adjustments.
4. Replace general data-room/public-register disclosure with a fair-disclosure standard; freeze and seal the data room as at 22 Sept 2026.
5. Delete cl 8.3 constructive knowledge; fall-back to actual knowledge of named individuals of matters fairly disclosed.
6. Bluefen: Buyer-only CP for unconditional consent **plus** satisfaction/waiver of cl 11.3 conditions; price protection if conditional.
7. DD-005 bonuses (grossed up for SG/payroll tax, ~AUD 490–500k) treated as Transaction Expense deducted from price.

**Strong push**
8. Ironquay: cleared payment **and** confirmatory IP assignment as Completion deliverable; specific indemnity for IP title defects, not limited to AUD 180k.
9. DD-006 incident: pre-Completion investigation/notification covenant; uncapped specific indemnity; bring-down and MAC right.
10. General cap: open at 50–100%, floor 30–40% absent W&I; tipping basket; lower de minimis; related-claim aggregation.
11. Escrow/retention 10–15% for 18–24 months (longer tail for tax/indemnities) or parent guarantee.

**Clean-up / diligence**
12. Sandbar renewals: determine accrual, necessity and timing; price or working-capital treatment accordingly.
13. Complete independent title verification (ASIC, PPSR, constitution, options/notes, certificates).
14. Lease notification evidence at Completion; Mossvale change-of-control check; general "no contract affected by the Transaction" warranty.
15. Separate tax indemnity and extended IP warranty survival.
